lede: The Persians had crushed the Byzantines and taken Jerusalem, and the idolaters of Makkah were jubilant. Then this surah came down and said that within a few years the outcome would be reversed. Abū Bakr staked a wager on it. It happened as it was said.

names.name: al-Rūm
names.note: After the people named in its second ayah — the Romans of the East, whose empire was ruled from Constantinople and who held Syria and Palestine. It is the only surah named after a foreign nation of the Prophet’s ﷺ own time.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan without any disagreement, as al-Qurṭubī says, and Ibn al-Jawzī records the agreement. Its opening is dated by the event it speaks of: the defeat of the Byzantines by the Persians “in the nearest land”, which took place in the middle years of the Prophet’s ﷺ mission. The traditional order places it eighty-fourth.
revelation.when: Makkah, some seven years before the Hijrah, when news came of the Persian conquest of Syria and Palestine

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الرُّومِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ الرُّومِ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّهَا مِنْ غَيْرِ خِلَافٍ، وهي ستون آية

setting: The two great powers of the age were at war. The Persians, under Khusraw, overran the Byzantine provinces of the Near East, took Damascus and then Jerusalem, and drove the emperor Heraclius back until, as Ibn Kathīr tells it, he was besieged in his own capital.

In Makkah the news divided people along a line they all understood. Ibn al-Jawzī gives it from the commentators: the Persians had no scripture, denied the Resurrection and worshipped idols; the Byzantines were a people of a Book. So the idolaters rejoiced and said to the Muslims: you are people of a scripture, and the Christians are people of a scripture; our brothers the Persians have beaten your brothers — and if you fight us, we shall beat you.

The surah came down: “The Byzantines have been defeated, in the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome — within a few years.” The word used, biḍʿ, means a number from three to nine. Abū Bakr went out and announced it, and the idolaters challenged him to a wager, in the days before such wagers were forbidden. He first fixed too short a term, and the Prophet ﷺ told him to lengthen it: “Why did you not make it less than ten?”

Nothing could have looked less likely. And yet within that span Heraclius struck back, broke the Persian armies and recovered what had been lost. Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī said: on the day of Badr the Byzantines prevailed over the Persians, and the believers were glad of it — as the ayah had said they would be: “and on that day the believers will rejoice, in the help of Allah.”

From that sign in history the surah turns to signs that need no news to carry them. Six times it says, “And among His signs…”: your creation from dust; mates made from yourselves, with affection and mercy placed between you; the difference of your tongues and colours; your sleep and your seeking of His bounty; the lightning and the rain; the standing of the heaven and the earth by His command.

occasions.title: Abū Bakr’s wager
occasions.text: The idolaters liked the Persians to prevail over the Byzantines, because they too were people of idols; the Muslims liked the Byzantines to prevail, because they were people of a Book. They mentioned it to Abū Bakr, and he to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: “They will indeed be victorious.” Abū Bakr told them, and they said: set a term between us. He set five years, and they did not prevail. He mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, who said: “Why did you not make it less than ten?”
occasions.source: Ibn ʿAbbās: Aḥmad and al-Tirmidhī (3193), who graded it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ gharīb. Ibn Kathīr gives it at the head of the surah.

evidence.quote: وَكَانَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ يُحِبُّونَ أَنْ تَظْهَرَ الرُّومُ عَلَى فَارِسَ؛ لِأَنَّهُمْ أَهْلُ كِتَابٍ، فذُكر ذَلِكَ لِأَبِي بَكْرٍ،، فَذَكَرَهُ أَبُو بَكْرٍ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ، فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ: "أَمَا إِنَّهُمْ سَيَغْلِبُونَ

aim: To set out the reality that governs the world: the turning of affairs, conditions and events belongs to Allah alone — “To Allah belongs the command, before and after.”
themes: The prophecy of the Byzantine victory

outline.title: The prophecy
outline.summary: Alif Lām Mīm. The Byzantines have been defeated in the nearest land; and they, after their defeat, will overcome, within a few years. To Allah belongs the command, before and after. On that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah. It is the promise of Allah. But most people do not know: they know what is apparent of the life of this world, and of the Hereafter they are heedless.

outline.title: Reflect, and travel
outline.summary: Have they not reflected within themselves? Allah created the heavens and the earth only in truth and for an appointed term. Have they not travelled the land and seen how those before them ended — who were stronger, and tilled the earth and built upon it more than these have? So glorify Allah when you reach the evening and when you rise in the morning. He brings the living out of the dead and the dead out of the living; and thus you will be brought out.

outline.title: “And among His signs”
outline.summary: Among His signs is that He created you from dust. Among His signs is that He created for you mates from yourselves, that you may find rest in them, and placed between you affection and mercy (30:21). Among His signs: the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the diversity of your tongues and colours; your sleep by night and day; the lightning, and the rain that gives life to the earth after its death; and that the heaven and the earth stand by His command.

outline.title: The upright religion
outline.summary: He sets you an example from yourselves: do you make your slaves equal partners in what We have given you? So set your face to the religion, inclining to truth — the natural disposition upon which Allah created mankind; there is no altering Allah’s creation. That is the upright religion. Turn to Him, and do not be of those who split their religion into sects. Give the kinsman his due, and the needy, and the traveller. What you give in usury does not increase with Allah; what you give in charity, seeking His Face, is multiplied.

outline.title: Corruption, wind and rain
outline.summary: Corruption has appeared on land and sea because of what people’s hands have earned, that He may make them taste some of what they have done, so that they may return. Among His signs is that He sends the winds as heralds of good news. Look at the traces of Allah’s mercy — how He gives life to the earth after its death. He it is who will give life to the dead. You cannot make the dead hear.

outline.title: Weakness, strength, weakness
outline.summary: It is Allah who created you in weakness, then after weakness gave strength, then after strength gave weakness and grey hair. On the Day the Hour arrives, the guilty will swear they stayed but an hour. So be patient: the promise of Allah is true. And do not let those who have no certainty shake you.

keyAyah.why: The sentence the whole surah explains. Before the defeat and after the victory, the command was His.

virtues.text: “No child is born but upon the natural disposition. Then his parents make him a Jew, or a Christian, or a Magian — as an animal brings forth its young whole: do you see any among them maimed?” Then Abū Hurayrah recited: “The natural disposition upon which Allah created mankind; there is no altering Allah’s creation.”
virtues.arabic: مَا مِنْ مَوْلُودٍ إِلاَّ يُولَدُ عَلَى الْفِطْرَةِ

virtues.text: “On the day of Badr the Byzantines prevailed over the Persians, and that pleased the believers. Then there came down: ‘Alif Lām Mīm. The Byzantines have been defeated…’ to ‘the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah.’”
virtues.grade: Ḥasan gharīb, said al-Tirmidhī; ṣaḥīḥ according to al-Albānī

before: Al-ʿAnkabūt ended: Allah is with those who do good. Al-Rūm opens with the believers’ side in the world losing — and the announcement that it will not stay so.
after: Al-Rūm ends: be patient; the promise of Allah is true. Luqmān opens with the Book of wisdom, and then the counsel of a wise man to his son: be patient over what befalls you.
